To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a novel effect system that can precisely compute effects at runtime, which enables precise concurrency between handlers, and we showed the soundness of this system.

(1) we present the first type-and-effect system that can statically analyze the effects of handlers at runtime, and (2) our system improves concurrency between handlers, and (3) our system can be applied to a wide range of event driven systems, and (4) we have implemented the system in a prototype tool and have evaluated it on a set of realistic examples.
we have designed a type-and-effect system to support modular and safe concurrency for asynchronous, typed event handlers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of an event system that is safe for concurrent execution.
the design, analysis and implementation of a novel effect system for asynchronous, dynamic event systems.
developing a formal framework for asynchronous events that can be used as a foundation for future event systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a type and effect system that enables precise concurrency reasoning in event driven systems.
we have developed a system to statically reason about the effects of event handlers, and that this system can be soundly and precisely used to improve concurrency in event systems.
our design provides a novel and practical approach to improve the concurrency safety of dynamic, asynchronous event systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
asynchronous, typed events is a novel, practical and safe system for asynchronous, concurrent event-driven systems.
we provide a formal basis for asynchronous, typed event systems, and show how to leverage runtime information to achieve precise and sound effect analyses.
asynchronous, typed events is a sound, modular and precise effect system for asynchronous, event-driven programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
runtime information can be used to improve the soundness and precision of static effect analyses.
runtime effect computation can improve concurrency between handlers in event driven systems.
the runtime information of handlers registration and the precomputed effects of handlers can be leveraged to improve concurrency.
